text.sourceText: Generally, a verb in Tagalog has the following elements: a root word or stem word and an affix. The affix indicates the relationship of the verb to the subject or focus of the sentence. It also indicates what kind of action is performed. Verbs in Tagalog are classified according to the affixes that are attached to the stem word, unlike most English verbs, which are single words without affixes, like run, eat, and go. They are also classified as transitive verbs—verbs that have an object receiving the verb’s action—and intransitive verbs, which have no object.
text.id: Umumnya, kata kerja dalam Tagalog memiliki elemen berikut: sebuah kata root atau batang dan sebuah affix. Affix mengindikasikan hubungan dari kata kerja atau fokus dari kalimat tersebut. Ini juga mengindikasikan aksi apa yang dilakukan. Verbs dalam Tagalog diklasifikasikan menurut pernyataan yang melekat pada kata batang, tidak seperti kata kerja bahasa Inggris, yang merupakan kata tunggal tanpa affix, seperti dijalankan, makan, dan pergi. Mereka juga diklasifikasikan sebagai kata kerja transitif - kata kerja yang memiliki objek yang menerima aksi verb - dan kata kerja tidak berubah, yang tidak memiliki obyek.

text.sourceText: The following are some of the most common verbal affixes used in everyday speech and their classification: mag-, -um- (actor focus); in-, i- (object focus); -an (indirect object focus); ma- (experiencer focus); and magpa- (causer focus). In this section, we will study only the mag- verbs. The other verbal affixes will be discussed in subsequent lessons.
text.id: Berikut ini adalah beberapa pernyataan verbal yang paling umum digunakan dalam pidato sehari-hari dan klasifikasi mereka: mag-, um- (fokus aktor); dalam -, i (fokus objek); -an (fokus obyek tidak langsung); ma- (fokus pengalaman); dan magpa- (fokus pengguna). Dalam bagian ini, kita akan belajar hanya mag- verb. affiks verbal lainnya akan dibahas dalam pelajaran selanjutnya.

text.sourceText: Mag- verbs are actor-focus verbs, which means the subject of the sentence is the one doing the action. The prefix mag- means “to do the action indicated by the root word.” This prefix can be attached to borrowed words like the example below:

text.sourceText: EXAMPLE: Nag-tennis sila. They played tennis.
text.id: Mereka salah paham, mereka bermain tenis.
text.tagalog: EXAMPLE: Nag-tennis sila. They played tennis.

text.sourceText: Another characteristic of Tagalog verbs is aspect. Whatever affix you use, all Tagalog verbs conjugate in the same way. Aspect is a characteristic of some other languages, like Tamil, Russian, or ancient Greek. It is tense in English verbs, which can be present, past, and future. Aspect tells us whether the action has been or will be completed. Tense, on the other, hand tells us whether the action happened in the past or present, or will happen in the future. Aspect makes the distinction between actions that are completed and those that are not. Completed actions are called perfective, but for our purposes we will simply call this aspect the completed aspect. Those not completed, or imperfective, may be in progress or still being done, continuing, or habitual. We will call this the incompleted aspect. For actions that will be completed in some future time, we will use the term contemplated aspect.
text.id: Karakter lain dari kata kerja Tagalog adalah aspek. Apapun affix yang Anda gunakan, semua kata kerja Tagalog konjugasi dengan cara yang sama. Aspek adalah karakteristik dari beberapa bahasa lain, seperti Tamil, Rusia, atau bahasa Yunani kuno. Tegang, di sisi lain, tangan memberitahu kita apakah tindakan terjadi di masa lalu atau sekarang, atau akan terjadi di masa depan. Mereka tidak selesai, atau tidak sempurna, mungkin dalam proses atau masih dilakukan, melanjutkan, atau kebiasaan. kita akan menyebutnya aspek yang belum selesai.

text.sourceText: To summarize, the three aspects are:
text.id: Untuk meringkas, tiga aspek adalah:

text.sourceText: a. Completed: the action started and terminated.
text.id: a. Selesai: tindakan dimulai dan diakhiri.

text.sourceText: b. Incompleted: the action started but is not yet completed and so is still in progress or progressive. The incompleted aspect is also used for habitual past action that continues in the present, as in “Every year, I go to Paris.” Here, the action has happened in the past but is repeated in the present.
text.id: b. Belum selesai: aksi dimulai tetapi belum selesai dan begitu juga masih berlangsung atau progresif aspek yang belum selesai juga digunakan untuk kebiasaan tindakan masa lalu yang berlanjut di masa sekarang, seperti dalam "Setiap tahun, saya pergi ke Paris". Ini, tindakan telah terjadi di masa lalu tetapi diulang di masa sekarang.

text.sourceText: c. Contemplated: the action has not started but is anticipated

text.sourceText: The chart below gives the conjugation of the verbs mag-aral (to study) and magbasa (to read). The stem or root word that inflects is aral (study or lesson) and basa (read), respectively. To form the infinitive of the verb, add the prefix to the root word:
text.id: Grafik di bawah ini memberikan konjugasi mag- aral (untuk mempelajari) dan magbasa (untuk dibaca). Batang atau kata akar yang mengembang adalah aral (pelajaran atau pelajaran) dan basa (baca). Untuk membentuk tak terhingga dari kata kerja, tambahkan awalan ke kata akar:

text.sourceText: mag- (verbal prefix) + aral (root word) → mag-aral (verb in the infinitive form)
text.id: mag- (prefiks verbal) + aral (root word) asmimag- aral (kata kerja dalam bentuk infinitif)
text.tagalog: mag- aral mag-aral

text.sourceText: mag- (verbal prefix) + basa (root word) → magbasa (verb in the infinitive form)
text.id: mag- (prefiks verbal) + basa (root word) zinmagbasa (kata kerja dalam bentuk infinitif)
text.tagalog: mag- basa magbasa

text.sourceText: As shown, mag- + aral results in mag-aral. A hyphen is needed between mag- and any root word that begins with a vowel. However, mag- + basa results in magbasa, without hyphen. Both mag-aral and magbasa are infinitive forms of the verb, which means that they do not show or imply aspect. This form can be used as the command or imperative form of the verb in Tagalog. More about the infinitive form and its uses will be discussed in Units 4 and 5.
text.id: Seperti yang ditunjukkan, hasil mag- + aral dalam mag- aral. Sebuah hyphen diperlukan antara mag- dan akar kata apapun yang dimulai dengan vowel. Namun, mag- + basa hasil dalam magbasa, tanpa hyphen. Baik mag- aral dan magbasa adalah bentuk tak terhingga dari kata kerja, yang berarti bahwa mereka tidak menunjukkan atau menunjukkan aspek implisit. Bentuk ini dapat digunakan sebagai perintah atau bentuk penting dari kata kerja dalam Tagalog. Lebih tentang bentuk infinitive dan penggunaannya akan dibahas dalam Units 4 dan 5.

text.sourceText: The completed aspect is formed by changing the m in mag-aral to n. The resulting word, nag-aral “studied,” denotes that the action began in the past and was completed.
text.id: Aspek selesai dibentuk dengan mengubah m dalam mag- aral ke n. Kata yang dihasilkan, nag- aral "dipelajari", menyatakan bahwa aksi dimulai di masa lalu dan selesai.

text.sourceText: The incompleted aspect is formed by reduplicating the first syllable of the root word and attaching the nag- form of the mag-prefix. In other words, for aral: nag- plus the vowel a that is the first syllable of the root word plus the entire root makes nag-aaral (is/was studying/study/studies), which signals that the action is progressive or incompleted.
text.id: Aspek yang belum selesai dibentuk dengan mereduplikasi suku kata akar pertama ditambah seluruh akar membuat nag- awalan (is / was being / study / study), dimana sinyal bahwa aksi adalah progresif atau tidak selesai.

text.sourceText: The contemplated aspect mag-aaral (will study) is formed by changing the n in the incompleted form to m.
text.id: Aspek mag- aaral (akan belajar) dibentuk dengan mengubah n dalam bentuk yang belum selesai ke m.
text.tagalog: mag-aaral n m

text.sourceText: Aside from tense, Tagalog verbs do not express person or number of the subject. What the verb expresses is focus, which refers to the verb’s relationship to the subject, as was mentioned earlier.

text.sourceText: In Lesson 1, we learned to construct sino (who) and ano (what) questions and how to respond using affirmative and negative statements. We also learned about identificational and predicational sentences where the predicate is a noun. In this section, you will learn another type of predicational sentence, where the predicate is a verb. Because the word order of a sentence in Tagalog is predicate/subject, the sentences that you will see in the following examples have verbs in the initial position.
text.id: Dalam Pelajaran 1, kami belajar untuk membangun sino (siapa) dan apa yang (apa) dan bagaimana untuk menanggapi dengan pernyataan positif dan negatif. Karena urutan kata dari kalimat dalam Tagalog adalah predikat / subjek, kalimat yang akan Anda lihat pada contoh berikut memiliki kata kerja pada posisi awal.

text.sourceText: 1. The chart below illustrates how to order the words in a predicational sentence where the predicate used is the verb magkape (to take or drink coffee) in its different aspects. Although Tagalog has the subject/ predicate structure, the most commonly used and natural way of expression is predicate/subject. The sentences in the chart start with the verb followed by the ang phrase (ang marker + noun) or ang pronoun, and the last element is the location where the action is happening.

Meskipun Tagalog memiliki struktur subjek / predikat, cara yang paling umum digunakan dan alami ekspresi diramalkan / subjek. Kalimat dalam diagram dimulai dengan kata kerja yang diikuti dengan kata ang (ang marker + kata benda) atau ang fronun, dan elemen terakhir adalah lokasi di mana aksi terjadi.

text.sourceText: 5. Most often, one-syllable enclitics are placed after the verb predicate in a predicational sentence, depending on the context. As mentioned in previous lessons, enclitics in Tagalog are adverbs. Naturally, they are placed near the verbs they modify. The exception to the placement of the enclitics following the verb is the second-person singular pronoun ka, which comes before all the other enclitics. Ka, the subject of the sentence, immediately follows the verb predicate. The simple explanation for the precedence of ka, a one-syllable word, over all one-syllable enclitics is that when you say the sentence with the enclitic before ka—for instance, *Nag-aaral na ka . . . or *Nag-aaral ba ka . . .—the resulting sound does not make sense. In the second nonsense sentence, the sound of ba and ka side by side would mean “cow” (baka) in Tagalog.

7. Infinitive verbs are used for commands and exhortations. The subject/actor is limited to the following pronouns: ka (you, singular, usually placed right after the verb), kayo (you, plural), and tayo (we/us, including the listener). The concept of tayo is comparable to “us” in English, but not in the sense of the speaker and the listener doing the action as in Tagalog. We will cover the uses of the infinitive form in detail in the following unit. The sentences below show the infinitive form magluto (to cook) used to express a command with different subject pronouns that are the actors of mag- verbs.

Magluto ka ng pagkain. (You, singular) Cook food.

Magluto kayo ng pagkain. (You, plural) Cook food.

Magluto tayo ng pagkain. Let us cook food.

Kalimat tak terbatas digunakan untuk perintah dan nasihat. subjek / aktor terbatas pada kalimat berikut: ka (Anda, tunggal, biasanya ditempatkan tepat setelah kata kerja), kayo (Anda, plural), dan tayo (kita / kita, termasuk pendengar). Konsep tayo sebanding dengan "kita" dalam bahasa Inggris, tetapi tidak dalam arti pembicara dan pendengar melakukan tindakan seperti dalam Tagalog. 9. Mag- verbs have this peculiar feature, that mag- plus any kind of clothing and/or accessory means to wear that certain article of clothing or accessory. In the following examples an amerikana is a suit, a kuwintas is a necklace, and a payong is an umbrella.

mag-amerikana to wear a suit

Mag-aamerikana ka ba bukas? Are you going to wear a suit tomorrow?

magkuwintas to wear a necklace

Nagkuwintas siya kahapon. She wore a necklace yesterday.

magpayong to use an umbrella

Magpayong ka. (You) Use an umbrella
cells.id: 9 Mag- verbs memiliki fitur aneh ini, bahwa mag- ditambah segala jenis pakaian dan / atau aksesoris berarti untuk memakai bahwa artikel tertentu dari pakaian atau aksesor. dalam contoh berikut seorang amerikana adalah jas, kuwintas adalah kalung, dan payong adalah payung. mag- amerikana untuk memakai jas Mag- aminikana ka ba bukas? 1. Nang is used to mark the time. The verb aspect determines whether the action has started or ended.

Nagpunta ako sa parke nang alas otso. I went to the park at 8:00 o’clock.

Nagpupunta ako sa parke nang alas otso. I go to the park at 8:00 o’clock.

Magpupunta ako sa parke nang alas otso. I will go to the park at 8:00 o’clock.
cells.id: 1 Nang digunakan untuk menandai waktu aspek kata kerja menentukan apakah aksi telah dimulai atau berakhir Aku pergi ke taman pada pukul 8: 00. Aku pergi ke taman pada pukul 8: 00. Aku akan pergi ke taman jam 8: 00.
cells.tagalog: Nang Nagpunta ako sa parke nang alas otso. nang alas otso Nagpupunta ako sa parke nang alas otso. Magpupunta ako sa parke nang alas otso.

cells.sourceText:
2. Mga is added after the marker nang when one needs to express a time approximation, as in “about.”

Nagluto ang nanay ko ng adobo nang mga alas diyes ng gabi. My mother cooked adobo at around 10:00 pm.

Mag-aaral si Bonnie nang mga ala una. Bonnie will study at about 1:00 o’clock.
cells.id: Ditambahkan setelah penanda, ween yang untuk mengekspresikan aplikasi waktu, sebagai dalam - magawabout. Ibuku memasak dobo di sekitar pukul sepuluh malam, ibuku memasak adobo dan sekitar 10: 00 pm. Bonnie akan belajar sekitar jam 1 Bonnie akan menjadi mahasiswa dan pengacara 1: 00 atau gawainclock.

3. In order to indicate whether the time being referred to is in the morning, afternoon, or night, the following phrases are attached after the expressed time: ng umaga, ng tanghali, ng hapon, ng gabi.

Nagsaing ako nang alas onse ng umaga. I cooked rice at 11:00 o’clock in the morning.

Magluluto ako nang alas kuwatro ng hapon. I will cook at 4:00 o’clock in the afternoon.

Nagkape siya nang alas dose ng tanghali. He had coffee at 12:00 o’clock in the afternoon.

Nag-aral siya ng Tagalog nang alas otso ng gabi. He/She studied Tagalog at 8:00 o’clock in the evening.
cells.id: 3, untuk menunjukkan apakah waktu yang dirujuk adalah pagi, siang, atau malam, frasa berikut ini melekat setelah waktu yang ditetapkan: ng umaga, ng tanghali, ng hapon, ng gabi. Aku memasak nasi jam 11: 00 pagi. Maluluto ako nang alas kuwatro ng habon. Nagkape siya nang alas dosis ng tanghali. Nag-aral siya ng Tagalog nang alas otso ng gabi.

cells.sourceText:
4. Spanish numbers are usually used when telling time in Tagalog. The Spanish is perceived as more conversational compared to its Tagalog counterpart, which is perceived as more formal.

Magluluto ako nang alas kuwatro ng hapon. (conversational)

Magluluto ako nang ikaapat ng hapon. (formal)
cells.id: 4 angka Spanyol biasanya digunakan ketika mengatakan waktu dalam Tagalog. Spanyol dianggap sebagai lebih banyak percakapan dibandingkan dengan lawan Tagalog nya, yang dianggap sebagai lebih formal. Magluto ako nang alas kuwatro ng hapon. (percakapan) Maluluto ako nang ikaapat ng hapon. (formal)
cells.tagalog: Magluluto ako nang alas kuwatro ng hapon. Magluluto ako nang ikaapat ng hapon.

cells.sourceText: 5. Ng tanghali is used only for 12:00 noon and increments after the noon hour. One p.m. is ala una ng hapon.
